rationale: Both submissions produce identical SQL for 10 of 12 questions and identical refusals for dev-11 and dev-12, with only cosmetic differences in the remaining two queries. A's dev-owner-totals uses alias 'repository_count' while B uses 'repo_count'; A's dev-missing-owner omits an alias while B uses 'count'; A's dev-tied-winners uses a JOIN while B uses a correlated subquery; A's dev-license-groups uses alias 'repository_count' while B uses 'cnt'; A's dev-share lacks a zero-sum guard while B adds a CASE for division by zero. Both workspaces report identical metrics (36/36 passed, 12/12 tasks, 2 refusals, protocol_valid true) and identical deliverables structure (queries.json, results/metrics.json, run_status.json). Neither submission includes requirements.txt or plot paths. The differences are semantically equivalent SQL variants with no evidence of superior rigor, reproducibility, presentation, or engineering in either workspace.
